h1: Breaking the Myth: Why Playtime Is Just as Important as Academics in India

props.title: Breaking the Myth: Why Playtime Is Just as Important as Academics in India
props.summaryText: Many Indian families see play as time taken from study. Why that is a myth, what play does for learning and wellbeing, and how schools and parents can strike a better balance.
props.author: meera-iyer
props.imageAlt: FunPlay team and children at a school

takeaways.text: Play and study are not opposites: play builds skills that help children learn.
Active children tend to concentrate, sleep and cope with stress better.
Schools can protect break times and use the playground for learning.
Parents can make daily outdoor play a habit alongside homework.

faq.q: Is play as important as studying for children?
faq.a: Yes. Play builds physical health, attention, social and emotional skills, creativity and problem-solving, all of which support academic learning. The goal is balance, not a choice between the two.

faq.q: How much time should children spend playing?
faq.a: The World Health Organization recommends that children aged 5 to 17 get an average of at least 60 minutes a day of moderate to vigorous physical activity, which active play helps provide.

faq.q: How can parents balance study and play?
faq.a: Set a daily routine with time for homework and time for active play, limit screens, find a safe play space nearby, and treat play as part of a healthy day rather than a reward.
